analysis:
Both units are head-side text from docs/architecture/inference.md, a documentation-only change. The patch updates the date, adds a Gemma 4 tensor-parallel placement note and a new Gemma 4 tensor-parallel foundation section, and renames a source path reference. I saw no code, configuration or control changes.

The visible text (lines 4512-5353) describes the encoded prefix-record tier and its binding of the encoding into the directory, record header and load agreement. It also covers paged KV, batch decode, media transport, MiMo, Gemma and Qwen tensor-parallel lanes, and observation logs.

Threat-model relevance:
- T-041 (prefix cache) and TB-007 (inference engine). The encoded record tier appears to stay inside the existing SSD tier controls. Records with another encoding are refused and deleted. The encoding is bound into the load agreement. Observation logs (`darkbloom-*-batch-decode-v1`, `memory-v1`) are described as size-only, with no tokens, logits or prompt text. I found no claim that weakens the T-041 posture such as HMAC names, the 30-minute TTL, or the DBK3 AAD. The doc states that older rows are approximate by contract, which is an integrity and accuracy note rather than a confidentiality regression.
- Media. Encoded media bytes are held only by the request owner and rank 0, and rank 1 gets metadata only. This is consistent with A-001 handling.

A hunk of the Gemma 4 tensor-parallel foundation section (new lines 4037-4240) lies outside the supplied unit text, so I did not review it. The wording on Gemma tensor-parallel placement at lines 3635-3638 is also outside these units. The next pass should check that those sections do not claim serving grants, qualification or new network or key-handling behavior that contradicts TB-002 or TB-011. I identified no security regressions. Whether the docs match the code is unverifiable without the code diffs.
